chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood on the mound on which the Masjid al-Fatah is located, during the Expedition of the Confederates, on a dark, cold night. He said: 'Who will go and bring us news of them, and for him is Paradise?' No one stood up. Then he repeated it, and no one stood up. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, gesturing with his hand: 'What the people wanted was something superior to Paradise.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Who is this?' He said, 'Hudhayfah.' He said: 'Do you not hear my speech since the night and do not speak? May you be buried (in the earth)?' So Hudhayfah stood up while saying: 'The cold and the hardship prevented me from answering you, may Allah make me your ransom.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Go until you hear their speech and bring me their news.' When he left, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, protect him from before him and behind him, from his right and from his left, until You return him.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Hudhayfah, do not narrate anything until you come to me.' So he took his sword, his bow, and his shield.
Hudhayfah said: 'I went out and I was not affected by hardship or cold. I passed by the Gate of the Ditch, which had been surrounded by the Believers and the Disbelievers.'

When Hudhayfah turned away, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) stood and called out: 'O Helper of the afflicted, and O Responder to the distressed, remove my anxiety, my grief, and my distress, for You see my condition and the condition of my companions.' Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended upon him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, verily Allah, Exalted is His mention, has heard your speech and your supplication, and has answered you and sufficed you against the terror of your enemy.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) knelt on his knees, extended his hands, shed tears, and then said: 'Thank You, thank You, as You have shown mercy to me and to my companions.'

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has sent upon them a wind from the lowest heaven containing gravel, and a wind from the fourth heaven containing large stones.'

Hudhayfah said: 'I went out and I saw the fires of the people. And the first army of Allah arrived: a wind containing gravel. It did not leave any of their fires except that it extinguished it, nor any tent except that it uprooted it, nor any spear except that it threw it away, until they were shielding themselves with their shields from the gravel, and we could hear the sound of the gravel striking the shields.'

Hudhayfah sat between two men from the Polytheists. Iblis appeared in the form of an authoritative man among the Polytheists and said: 'O people, you have encamped in the vicinity of this sorcerer and liar. Indeed, nothing of his affair will escape you, for it has not been a year of staying put. The shoes and the hooves have been destroyed. So return, and let every man among you look at who is his companion.'
Hudhayfah said: 'I looked to my right, tapped him with my hand, and said: Who are you? He said: Muawiya. I said to the one on my left: Who are you? He said: Suhayl ibn Amr.'

Hudhayfah said: 'And the greatest army of Allah arrived. Abu Sufyan rose to his camel, then shouted among the Quraysh: 'Safety, safety!' And Talhah al-Azdi said: 'Muhammad has increased your evil.' Then he rose to his camel and shouted among the Banu Ashja': 'Safety, safety!' Uyayna ibn Hisn did the same. Then al-Harith ibn Awf al-Muzani did the same. Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis did the same. And the Confederates departed, and Hudhayfah returned to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and informed him of the news.'
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It was indeed resembling the Day of Judgment for them.'

key_terms.جُنْدُ اللَّهِ: The Army of Allah (divine forces or angels)
key_terms.حُذَيْفَةُ: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, the companion known for his knowledge of the hypocrites and his role as a scout
key_terms.غَزْوَةُ الْأَحْزَابِ: Expedition of the Confederates (Battle of Khandaq)

ai.seo_question: What happened during the Battle of the Confederates regarding the Prophet's scout and the divine wind?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the Battle of the Confederates, highlighting Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman’s role as the Prophet’s scout and the subsequent divine wind that scattered the enemy camp. It uniquely connects this historical event to eschatological themes, with Imam al-Sadiq noting the resemblance of the chaos to the Day of Judgment, while also identifying key future figures like Muawiya and Suhayl ibn Amr among the confederates. The narrative underscores the interplay between human agency, divine protection, and the cosmic significance of the Ghazwat al-Ahzab in Shia historiography.
